These nine CSVs are SYNTHETIC TEST FIXTURES, not the Olist dataset. Generated by
`python scripts/make_fixtures.py`. Four orders, four items, four payment records,
two customer records sharing one customer_unique_id, duplicate review IDs and
identical review/geolocation rows exercise grain and uniqueness assumptions.

Hand calculations: item sales 100+50+80+20 = BRL 250; freight 10+5+8+2 = BRL 25;
recorded payments 100+65+88+22 = BRL 275. The first order has two items AND two
payment records; a direct join would inflate its amounts. Books = 100+20 = 120;
Unknown = 50+80 = 130. Three delivered statuses; only two known delivery durations,
10 and 5 days. One of those two is late (50%). Placed-order AOV = 250/4 = 62.50.
Credit-card record share = 2/4 = 50%; value share = 188/275*100;
order share = 2/3*100 (orders without payments excluded by this definition).
